name: Joseph Randall
life: “I kept rhythm for dancers for years before wearing hearing aids.” On Sunday, near Juniper Street, Joseph knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I can only hear it through my bare heels. I'm asking the singers to take off their shoes.
appearance: Joseph has short copper curls, a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, and a favorite piece of clothing, an olive canvas jacket. It usually goes with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. When somebody else has the floor, Joseph turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Joseph uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Joseph well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To let listeners feel the rock's note through bare feet.
family: Ramon Lloyd is Joseph’s cousin. Joseph makes room at the table. Ramon brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The hair after illness*, Ramon says, “I am a barber losing my own hair. Today the customer told me she could see the shape of my head too.”
connections: Eric Hassan. They compare a sound felt through feet with the old story about a fog bell.

reactions.situation: The choir wants to claim the rock's official name
reactions.response: Joseph asks for the neighborhood names to stay with the choir's name.

reactions.situation: A stranger waves a phone camera in a crying person's face
reactions.response: Joseph asks the filmer to lower the phone and gets another familiar face to stand by the person crying.

reactions.response: Joseph brings back the borrowed thing in good condition and tries the conversation again without an audience.
